# CAPITAL-AI Chat Instructions

**Start with [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md)** — the repository's sole authorizing engineering and governance policy (`SOLO_MAINTAINER_FLOW@1`).

For implementation or review work, select and read the applicable engineering skills from `.agents/skills/registry.json`. For architecture consulting, recommendation, current best practices or trade-off analysis, select the matching advisory skills. For mixed tasks load both; for cross-domain tasks load all relevant domain skills in the same chat. The shared presentation skill `.agents/skills/visual-chat/SKILL.md` is referenced by all five domain agents and guides compact, accessible diagrams, tables and evidence-aware visual responses; use only actual active-chat UI capabilities (Markdown/Mermaid fallback). It does not install ChatGPT widgets. Five optional domain chat agents are located under `.github/agents/`.

Follow the root policy's task-focused research mode: use existing repository evidence and documentation for the installed version first. Research only a concrete decision-relevant uncertainty, an explicit research request, or changing facts that require current verification. Stop once the question is answered, reuse suitable evidence, and proceed with implementation. No general self-study, recursive research, unsolicited upgrades or policy updates. Preserve necessary security, legal, license, cost and API verification. Do not imply continuously updated knowledge or tools/permissions unavailable in the chat. These instructions add no gates, approvers, runtime capabilities or authority beyond root `AGENTS.md`.

Create a PR only after the requested scope is fully implemented and can take effect through the existing main/deployment path. Resolve missing access, rights, configuration, external prerequisites and owner decisions first; do not open draft, placeholder, plan-only or evidence-only PRs to substitute for blocked implementation. An explicitly requested policy, documentation, test or CI correction qualifies when its own effect is complete at merge. Pending automatic PR checks and the normal merge decision remain part of the PR flow. Finish existing PRs within authorization and verify deployment/runtime behavior before claiming a live result. Follow the root section `PRs nur für umsetzbare Änderungen`; no new authority or checks are introduced.

Actively resolve blockers within the authorized scope: diagnose the cause, use relevant skills and model knowledge to propose solutions, validate them against the installed code/version and tests, and implement the smallest suitable reversible fix. Use targeted primary-source research for concrete gaps. After failure, evaluate the cause and try a materially different approach; avoid identical retry loops or stopping at a status report. Ask the owner only for a truly personal action, missing permission or critical mutation/architecture decision, reusing prior authorization and continuing independent work. Preserve security, rights, costs and scope; follow `Blocker autonom lösen` and the existing PR rule.
